parts.visual:
A PR Scandal hits. The media is calling. Twitter is raging. The executive team must execute the Crisis Playbook.

The Playbook:
1. Assemble the War Room: Legal, PR, and the CEO in one room.
2. Freeze Outbound Comms: Stop all scheduled marketing tweets/emails immediately. Read the room.
3. The Holding Statement: Issue a brief statement acknowledging the issue while you gather facts.
parts.audio: When a scandal hits, assemble the War Room, freeze all scheduled marketing, and issue a Holding Statement. Never go silent.

questions.question: A major scandal breaks about your company. Why must you immediately 'Freeze Outbound Comms'?
options: Because you run out of internet data.
Because if your scheduled, cheerful marketing tweet goes out during a tragedy or scandal, your brand looks insanely tone-deaf and cruel.
questions.correct_answer: Because if your scheduled, cheerful marketing tweet goes out during a tragedy or scandal, your brand looks insanely tone-deaf and cruel.
questions.explanation: Automated marketing is dangerous during a crisis. Hit the kill switch instantly.

questions.question: Listen to the PR Director. What type of statement is this?
questions.tts_text: We are aware of the allegations and are currently conducting a full internal investigation. We take this very seriously.
questions.explanation: A Holding Statement buys you time. It tells the public 'We are awake and working on it' without committing to facts you don't have yet.

questions.question: Why is 'No Comment' the worst possible phrase to say to the media during a scandal?
options: It implies guilt and makes it look like you are hiding something.
questions.correct_answer: It implies guilt and makes it look like you are hiding something.
questions.explanation: If you don't control the narrative, the media will create the narrative for you. Never say 'No Comment'. Say 'We are currently investigating.'

questions.question: During a crisis, who should be the primary spokesperson for the company?
options: Any employee who wants to talk.
One single designated executive (usually the CEO or VP of PR) to ensure a unified, controlled message.
questions.correct_answer: One single designated executive (usually the CEO or VP of PR) to ensure a unified, controlled message.
questions.explanation: Mixed messaging during a crisis creates chaos. Lock down all unauthorized internal communication with the press.

pairs.match: A temporary statement issued to buy time during a crisis
A centralized command center for managing a crisis
Demonstrating a lack of understanding of public sentiment
The only individual authorized to speak on behalf of the company
